properties.name: The residual 29.6s was 7.6x redundant store reads: 108 region walks made 4,502 node visits over 589 distinct nodes, each visit paying two prefix scans for adjacency already read
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, the second half of the `design_regions` investigation. `fact:propagate-from-recomputed-an-all-pairs-betweenness-on-every-call-and-that-was-the-whole-cost` took it from never-returning to 29.6 s; its closing line said 29.6 s was still slow for a check-in read and that the remaining cost was the walks themselves. This is what those walks were doing.

    108 walks                     4,502 node visits
    distinct nodes ever visited     589
    redundancy                      7.6x
    ~4 ms a visit                  18.0 s of the 21.6 s spent walking

⭐ THE REGIONS OVERLAP, AND THE TOOL SAYS SO ITSELF. `design_regions`' own coverage block reports 589 of 846 covered nodes lying in MORE THAN ONE region — a fact it computes and reports while the code around it re-walks every one of them per seed. The evidence for the cause was already in the reply.

FOUR CANDIDATES, and three were refuted by measurement:
  · the observation is wrong / it was startup — REFUTED: re-timed fully warm at 30.0 s.
  · my own memo clones a 4,150-entry map per call — REFUTED: a zero-edge seed costs 5 ms, so fixed per-call overhead is negligible. Region cost tracks region SIZE (230–255 ms for ~60 nodes; 5–7 ms for 0–1).
  · the walks are simply N × a fair cost — PARTLY TRUE and not the whole story: 108 isolated warm walks cost 21.6 s of the 30.0 s, which is where the time was, but 7.6x of that work was redundant.
  · overlapping regions re-read the same adjacency — CONFIRMED by counting visits against distinct nodes.

⚠️ A COUNT THAT SILENTLY MEASURED NOTHING, caught before it was believed: the first redundancy count returned 108 visits over 108 distinct nodes, a tidy 1.0x. `propagate_from` summarises unless `full: true`, so the loop was reading an absent `impacted` list and counting zeros. The skill's step ⑤ is exactly this — a call that completed is not a call that worked.

THE CLASS: per-node store I/O inside a traversal, repeated across traversals that share nodes. `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times` makes the same argument one level coarser for `detect_defects` — build once, interrogate N times — and it reaches neither `propagate_from` nor this. Whether that Constraint should be widened to cover traversal inputs generally is a question for its owner.

BOUNDS. Debug binary; a release build is ~2.2x faster and would not change the ratio, which is a count rather than a duration. The adjacency is held per write generation and is invalidated by any write — pinned by a test that a newly written EDGE is visible to the next walk, because a cache that outlived a write would hide a real dependency, which is worse than any latency. Memory is bounded by edge count (24,242 here) and was not measured on a larger design. 12.5 s is still not fast: what remains is ~6.5 s of walking plus the three rollups paid once, and whether that is acceptable for a check-in read is a judgement nobody has made.
